og.title: Manufacturing and Materials Joining Innovation Center (Ma2JIC)
og.description: The Manufacturing and Materials Joining Innovation Center (Ma2JIC) develops advanced manufacturing technology associated with materials joining and metal additive manufacturing. Research projects use a mix of computational and experimental tools to achieve objectives and meet the needs of its broad-based industrial membership.Ma2JIC's mission is to advance the science and technology of advanced manufacturing as it applies to materials joining and metal additive manufacturing (printing). The goals are to:Develop scientifically based methodologies for assessing material weldability and printability that span nanometer (nm) to millimeter (mm) length scales.Close the gap between materials innovation and manufacturability.Develop experimental and computational tools for materials joining and advanced manufacturing.Develop a new generation of materials joining and additive manufacturing engineers and scientists.Materials joining and additive manufacturing are important aspects of advancing manufacturing, particularly in the context of incorporating advanced materials into the manufacturing of new products. Issues arise where the application of new materials (including printed) have been limited, or precluded, by an inability to join them. A basic problem on the path from development to implementation is the lack of a structured, scientifically based methodologies for determining material weldability and printability. The concept of weldability/printability occurs at the intersection of the joining/printing process and the materials' response to the thermal and mechanical conditions that are imposed by the processes. Considering the diverse need for materials in virtually every industry segment, it is critical to develop scientific methodologies to join and print these materials.

checks.label: HTTPS (required for service workers)
checks.why: HTTPS is required for service workers and most install prompts.

checks.label: Web app manifest declared
checks.why: A web app manifest is required for installability and controls how the app appears when launched.

checks.label: Service worker registered
checks.why: A service worker is what makes offline access, caching, and background sync possible.

checks.label: Theme color declared
checks.why: Theme color controls the browser chrome/status-bar color when the site is installed or bookmarked.

checks.label: Apple touch icon (iOS/bookmark icon)
checks.why: iOS uses this icon for home-screen bookmarks and "Add to Home Screen" — without it the icon falls back to a screenshot.

checks.label: Manifest fetched and parsed successfully
checks.why: A manifest that fails to parse cannot drive installability or launch behavior even if the link is present.

checks.label: Manifest declares a maskable icon
checks.why: A maskable icon lets the OS safely crop/mask the app icon on different device shapes without clipping content.

checks.label: Service worker is active (not just registered)
checks.why: An active service worker (not just registered) is what actually intercepts requests and serves cached content.

checks.label: Service worker controls this page load
checks.why: A controlling service worker means THIS page load is being served/intercepted, not just a future one.

checks.label: Meets basic installability criteria
checks.evidence: no readable web app manifest; no service worker registered
checks.why: Determines whether the browser can realistically offer "Add to Home Screen" / install, based on manifest + service worker + HTTPS together.
